subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which type of force acts to stretch or pull a material apart?
questions.explain: Tension is a pulling force that stretches a material, as in a rope holding a load.

questions.q: Which technique uses triangle shapes to make a frame structure more rigid and resistant to distortion?
questions.explain: Triangulation adds diagonal members to form triangles, which cannot be pushed out of shape like squares can.

questions.q: Movement backwards and forwards in a straight line is known as which type of motion?
questions.explain: Reciprocating motion repeats back and forth in a straight line, such as a piston or a sewing-machine needle.

questions.q: The turning effect of a force about a pivot is calculated using which formula?
options: Moment = force x perpendicular distance from pivot
questions.explain: A moment equals the applied force multiplied by its perpendicular distance from the pivot, measured in newton metres (Nm).

questions.q: An electronic system is commonly modelled using which three basic blocks?
questions.explain: The systems approach describes electronics as input (sensing), process (decision) and output (action) blocks.

questions.q: A light-dependent resistor (LDR) is used as an input component to detect changes in what?
questions.explain: An LDR is a light sensor whose resistance changes with the amount of light falling on it.

questions.q: Which force acts to squash or crush a material, such as the load on a table leg?
questions.explain: Compression is a pushing force that squashes a material, for example the downward load carried by a column.

questions.q: When a horizontal beam is loaded in the middle and supported at both ends, what happens to the material along the top and bottom surfaces?
options: The top is in compression and the bottom is in tension
The top is in tension and the bottom is in compression
questions.explain: A loaded beam sags, squashing the upper surface (compression) and stretching the lower surface (tension).

questions.q: A wheelbarrow is an example of which class of lever?
options: Second class, with the load between the fulcrum and the effort
First class, with the fulcrum between the load and the effort
Third class, with the effort between the fulcrum and the load
Second class, with the effort between the fulcrum and the load
questions.explain: In a wheelbarrow the wheel is the fulcrum, the load sits between it and the handles, making it a second-class lever.

questions.q: A small driver gear turns a larger driven gear. Compared with the driver, the driven gear will turn how?
options: More slowly but with more torque
More quickly but with less torque
At the same speed and torque
More quickly and with more torque
questions.explain: Driving a larger gear reduces output speed while increasing turning force (torque).

questions.q: A rotating cam acting on a follower is used to convert rotary motion into which type of motion?
questions.explain: As the cam rotates, its profile lifts and lowers the follower, producing up-and-down reciprocating motion.

questions.q: Why is a thermistor a suitable input component for a temperature-controlled system?
options: Its resistance changes as temperature changes
It stores charge as temperature rises
It switches direction of current with temperature
questions.explain: A thermistor's resistance varies with temperature, so it can sense heat and be used as a temperature input.

questions.q: How does laminating thin layers of material together increase the strength of a component?
options: Bonding several thin layers resists bending better than one layer of the same thickness
It removes all tension from the material
It makes the material lighter so it cannot break
It turns compression forces into tension forces
questions.explain: Lamination bonds layers, often with grains crossed, to resist bending and distribute stress, as in plywood.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of using a programmable microcontroller as the process block in a product?
options: Its behaviour can be changed by reprogramming without rewiring the circuit
It removes the need for any power supply
It works only with a single fixed output
It cannot respond to input signals
questions.explain: A microcontroller's function is set in software, so the same hardware can be reused for different tasks by reprogramming.

questions.q: A force of 20 N is applied at a perpendicular distance of 0.5 m from a pivot. What is the moment?
questions.explain: Moment = force x distance = 20 N x 0.5 m = 10 Nm.

questions.q: A lever lifts a load of 200 N using an effort of 50 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
A driver gear with 10 teeth rotates at 100 rpm and drives a gear with 40 teeth. What is the output speed of the driven gear?
questions.explain: Output speed = input speed x (driver teeth / driven teeth) = 100 x (10/40) = 25 rpm.

questions.q: A designer needs a garden light that switches on automatically when it becomes dark. Which input sensor should be used?
questions.explain: An LDR detects falling light levels, allowing the system to switch the light on when darkness falls.
